segments.text: Good Evening, This is Aakashwani, I am Shagun Chopra with the news at 9.
The Headlines
Prime Minister Narendra Modi to launch development projects worth over 14,000 crore rupees from
Banaskatha in Gujarat tomorrow to also release 24th installment of PM Kisan scheme amounting
to 19,000 crore rupees.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal says proposed India-US trade deal will protect farmers'
his interests and give country a competitive advantage. Finance Ministry projects countries
GDP growth at 7.35% in second quarter of current fiscal. Supreme Court says banks must compensate
digital fraud victims in case of negligence. IMD issues read alert for very heavy to extremely
heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow. And Indian wrestler Manisha advances to women's 59
KG final at World Championships in Kazakhstan.
Now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat beginning tomorrow.
Mr. Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development
projects worth over 14,000 crore rupees in Banaskar tomorrow.
The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase 2A Airport
extension and Phase 2B Gift City extension.
He will also release the 24th installment under PM Kisan, amounting to Rs.19,000 crore.
He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology in Vitro Fertilization Laboratory and the
Bharat Burvain Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskatha.
The centre will strengthen Burvain breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive
technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10 to 20 times.
Thereafter, the Prime Minister will travel to Aik Tanagar, Ke Vadia and inaugurate Bharat
Parv 2026.
On Saturday, Prime Minister Modi will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity.
Mr. Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various
development projects worth over 400 crore rupees in Aik Tanagar.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Koyal has said that India's proposed trade deal
with the United States will protect farmers' interests and give the country a competitive
advantage. He assured that the agreement would not compromise the sensitive interests of farmers
or any other stakeholders. Mr. Goyal was addressing the three-day national conference
on India's industrial transformation in New Delhi today.
The U.S. free trade deal is sometimes sought to be politicized by a few elements. But
I had the courage of conviction to announce, boldly, that the US trade deal, once details
are out, the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our
farmers or any stakeholder has been compromised.
The minister also said India has signed nine trade agreements covering 38 developed nations
with a combined GDP of $60 trillion.
Indian dollars. India's economic momentum remains strong with the economy projected
to grow by 7.35% in the second quarter of the financial year 2026-2027. According to
the Finance Ministry's monthly economic review for October released today, growth is supported
by stronger industrial output, higher energy consumption, increased port traffic, robust
GST collections and rising automobile sales. Here is a report.
The report highlighted that country's external sector continued to demonstrate resilience
last month amid heightened global uncertainty with total exports of merchandise and services
growing by 11% year-on-year. Merchandise exports, which grew by over 23% year-on-year, were
the principal driver of this growth led by electronics and engineering goods. Supported
by steady services surplus the overall trade deficit narrowed during the period.
The report noted that robust domestic demand, sustained investment activity, a resilient financial
sector and proactive supply-side management have underpinned India's growth resilience
so far.
It said amidst elevated crude oil prices, higher food inflation, an uncertain outlook
look for the creep crop, sustaining economic activity while safeguarding price stability
will be the focus of policy makers in the second half of the financial year.
Anupam Mish, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The Supreme Court has said banks and other financial institutions must be held accountable
for losses suffered by victims of digital fraud.
The court observed that victims of offenses such as digital arrest camps should receive
compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a
financial institution's failure to exercise due diligence.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Khanth and Justices Joy Malia Bakshi and Vee Mohunas
said, it will examine the Reserve Bank of India's proposed Know Your Customer or KVIC
Amendment Directions 2026.
The directions are expected to be notified by 30th of November and made operational
by 31st of December.
The National Eligibility Come Entrance Test for Superspecialty, NEED SS 2026, will be
conducted on December 11th and 12th this year.
In a notice issued today, the National Board of Examinations and Medical Sciences, NBAMS,
said the examination would be held in computer-based mode at various examination centres across
the country.
The last date for submitting the application form is November 18th this year.
The Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda has said that India has
made significant progress in healthcare and digital service delivery over the past 10
years.
Addressing a function in New Delhi today, Mr. Nadda said the number of aims has increased
from 1 Institute to 23 and the number of medical colleges has risen from 387 to 863.
He said through the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, the health records, vaccination
nation and screening of crores of people are being digitized so that health services can
become more accessible, effective and transparent.
Mr. Nadeh highlighted that 98 crore Aabha cards have been generated so far.
In this Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, we have started the Aabha card.
Aabha is Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts.
Every individual will have a card and you will be happy to note that about 98 crores
Aabha cards have been generated.
And to join this with medical health records, one-twenty-three crores have been linked with
the health records.
So this is how we are digitizing and we are trying to go forward."
Aayushman Vaivandana Yojna completed two years today.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the scheme in October 2024 to extend the benefits
of Aayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Janarogue Yojna to all citizens aged 70 years and
reserve, irrespective of their socioeconomic status.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said, the scheme aims to provide dignified, cashless
healthcare coverage to around six crore eligible senior citizens.
World Stroke Day is being observed today to raise awareness about stroke and the importance
of recognizing its warning signs.
This year's campaign message, Every Minute Counts, Know the Signs of Stroke, reminds
everyone that timely action can save lives.
On the occasion, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakashna Das said,
sudden facial drooping, weakness in an arm, or difficulty speaking, should never be ignored.
Talking to Akashwani News, Chief of the Neurosciences Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences
Ames, New Delhi, Dr. Shailesh B. Gaikwad said,
The symptoms of the stroke include sudden loss or blurring of vision, double vision, loss of balance, and difficulty in walking.
Dr. Gayakwar emphasized, if such symptoms are visible, then the patient should immediately
transfer to stroke-ready hospital for treatment.
There are some symptoms which should be recognized by the general people.
The term FAST has been propagated by the World Stroke Organization to create awareness
in order to recognize the earliest signs of the stroke.
In fast, the F stands for face where the face is stroking on one side, A stands for arm
or leg where there is a sudden onset of weakness, S stands for difficulty in speech, T stands
for time to act and reach to a hospital which is stroked ready.
You are listening to news at 9 on Akashwani.
Want more news? Follow us on X at AIR news alerts and subscribe to news on air official
on YouTube.
The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab over South Chattisgarh in adjoining South
Odisha has moved northwards. It is now centred over Central Chattisgarh in adjoining Odisha.
The Indian Meteorological Department, IMD said it is likely to move further north
and weakened into a well-marked, low-pressure area over North Chhattisgarh tonight.
Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.
In addition, torrential rain following Cyclone Arnab
has triggered severe flooding and landslides in Ganjam, Gajpati
and Kandamal districts, leaving dozens of villages marooned.
More from our correspondent.
Incessant rainfall following Cyclone Arnab has affected nearly 300 villages in Ganjam
District with around 70 reported marooned.
More than 2,000 people have been stranded, particularly in Sana Khemundi, Asuka, Dharakot,
Soroda, and Patrapur blocks.
The Resikulya River at Pursatampur has risen to 19 meters above its danger level of 16.8
meters.
The Bahuda and Bansatha rivers are also in spate.
Barampur has witnessed severe water logging while a stretch of National Highway 326 in
Gajapati has been washed away, cutting road connectivity.
The Indian coast guard has begun helicopter vacations, while rescue teams are assisting
affected people.
The East Coast Railway has cancelled 20 trains, and many other trains have been affected.
The IMD has warned of further rain in Odisha.
A new low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea is likely to intensify into a depression
around this Saturday.
Prakash Das, Prakashwani News, Bhuvaneswar.
Heavy rain continued across Chhattisgarh today under the influence of cyclone Annab.
As a precautionary measure, schools in several districts of the state have been closed till
tomorrow.
A report.
Cyclonic storm Arnab has wakened into a low-pressure area.
It is expected to move towards Northern Chhattisgarh over the next 12 hours.
As a result, rain is occurring today in several districts across Central and Northern Chhattisgarh.
The Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for certain districts within
in the Sarguja, Bilaspur and Raiapur divisions, while a red alert has been issued to Raiagad
and its surrounding areas. In the Bustal division, district including Sukhma, has been experiencing
rainfall for the past two days. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke with Chhattisgarh
Chief Minister Vishnu Deosai over the phone today to assess the current situation in
the state in light of the cyclone.
Rahul Sinha, Akashwani News, Raipur.

Lappara village, he directed officials to restore damaged houses and address fishermen's
boat registration issues. Mr. Naidu said a central team would visit the state tomorrow to
assess the damage. Year-end hope minister Amisha has assured full support from the center.
Raul Saiguresh, Akashwani News, Vijayawada.
An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh,
Sabhimal in West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nekobar Islands tomorrow.
Indian wrestler Manisha Bhanwala advanced to the women's 59kg final at the world championships
in Astana, Kazakhstan today. Manisha defeated home favorite Altin Shagayeva by a dominant
10-0 by fall to book her spot in the gold medal bout. She will face Abhagel Net of
the United States in the final tomorrow. Meanwhile, Tanusharma won the bronze medal
in the women's 72kg category after defeating Precious Bell of the United States 9-5.
In hockey, Indic continued their winning streak at Men's Asian Champion's Trophy by defeating
China 5-2 in their second league match at Jalandhar in Punjab this evening.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi to launch development projects worth over 14,000 crore rupees from
Naskata in Gujarat tomorrow to also release 24th installment of PM Kisan's scheme amounting
to Rs 19,000 crore.
Union Minister Piyush Koyal says proposed India-US trade deal will protect farmers' interests
and give country a competitive advantage.
Finance Ministry projects country's GDP growth at 7.35% in second quarter of current fiscal.
Supreme Court says banks must compensate digital fraud victims in case of negligence.
IMD issues read alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.
And Indian wrestler Manisha advances to women's 59kg final at world championships in Kazakhstan.
That is all in the news at 9.
Good night.
